StoryNodes.title: Bralizzar — The Charter
StoryNodes.player_narrative:
Bralizzar had seen expeditions before. Most arrived loudly, bought too much rope, too little water, and spoke of the Raurin as though the desert were an empty space waiting to be crossed. The six gathered in the shaded upper room of the caravan house knew better. They had already bled together once, defending a Sandvoyager caravan from servants of Set, and that fight had turned several separate loyalties into one company.

They called themselves the Seekers of Ra. The name was less an order than a promise: meet danger in the light, remember the dead, and do not confuse faith with carelessness. Ra—Amun-Ra in the temple rites most familiar to them—stood at the center of their shared devotion, while each honored other gods according to calling and conscience. Martek was different. His name lived in prophecy, old histories, and fragments whose meaning remained uncertain. None of them needed to pretend certainty before the evidence existed.

Around the table, each companion made his or her reason for being there visible without a speech. Malek checked the fastening on his scimitar and the straps that might have to hold under another charge. Vaelis turned a route sketch toward the window until the morning light matched the bearings on the page. Syrra examined the seals on the recovered fragment more closely than she examined the sponsors. Tal copied a damaged line of script into his journal before anyone could smudge it. Zarek counted water, feed, rope, arrows, and then counted them again. Snogard had the charter, the fragment, and the responsibility of deciding what came next—but his choices remained his own.

The summons had come through two doors at once: the Temple of Amun-Ra and the House of Martek. Old Martek-related prophecies had resurfaced in Bralizzar, incomplete and contradictory, and Set's followers had shown enough interest in related material to make coincidence difficult to believe. The sponsors did not ask the Seekers to conquer the desert. The first charge was smaller: ride to the frontier, learn why a boundary patrol near a cave had stopped reporting, judge whether the road beyond remained usable, and return with evidence that could be trusted.

Their reasons overlapped without being identical. Malek saw people who might need protection. Vaelis saw an edge of the map that had stopped being reliable. Syrra saw Set's shadow where others saw coincidence. Tal saw history in danger of being turned into rumor. Zarek saw six lives that would depend on water, animals, discipline, and a retreat route. Snogard's reasons would be defined by the player, not the narrator.

Before departure, the room fell briefly quiet as the first full light reached the eastern wall. That silence—more than any speech—was the Seekers' oldest shared prayer.

At dawn, the Seekers of Ra rode out.

StoryNodes.title: The Last Camp Before the Cave
StoryNodes.player_narrative:
By the final evening before the frontier cave, Bralizzar felt much farther away than the map suggested. The caravan road had narrowed to a hard ribbon between wind-cut stone and open desert. The patrol's last marker stood where it should, but the next signal cairn had not been renewed. No smoke rose ahead.

The camp settled into the habits that already distinguished them. Malek checked straps he had already checked, because someone else might depend on them. Vaelis watched the horizon through the last red light and marked the day's route without pretending the map knew more than it did. Syrra returned from the edge of camp with nothing dramatic to report, which somehow made everyone more attentive. Tal copied the patrol mark into his journal and preserved the name attached to it. Zarek counted animals, water skins, rations, rope, and arrows before allowing himself to sit.

As the sun disappeared, no one delivered a sermon. Their shared faith lived in smaller things: water passed before it was drunk, the dead named rather than forgotten, equipment made ready before prayer became an excuse for carelessness. Martek's prophecies were still evidence to be tested, not a theology already settled.

Snogard had the charter in his pack and five companions whose reasons for being here were different but compatible. What he chose to make of those reasons remained his decision.

At first light, the company would perform its brief sunrise observance and then approach the cave.

Beyond the camp, the desert waited in silence.

StoryNodes.title: Bralizzar — Expedition Business
StoryNodes.player_narrative: Bralizzar is prepared as the expedition's next staging and information chapter. On arrival, the immediate source-bound business is to meet Aman Al-Raqib, review outfitting, and establish readiness to depart toward Northknife Pass. The scene does not assume a combat encounter, invented city geography, or unsupported dialogue.
